title: L3 Dependency Choice Output
description: One decision row per candidate IG, rejected ones included, naming which profiles, value sets and libraries are reused, derived from or not used, and the ig-artifact-ingestion index each decision was read from.

indexes.description: One ig-artifact-ingestion index per candidate IG.

dependencyChoice.title: Dependency choice
dependencyChoice.description: The output of a dependency-choice stage (3 at L2, 5 at L3): one row per candidate, rejected ones included, the gaps, and the question put to the adjudicator. Defined by the l2-dependency-choice output contract and copied inline wherever it is passed on; the stage chain check compares the copies.

gaps.description: Candidates missing packageId, version or uri (DependsOnGap), each with what is missing.

decisionRequest.description: Path or URL of the DecisionRequest (cat-harness schemas/decision-request.ts) the adjudicator answers. Under the QA rule the agent has already gone on with its recommendation.

dependencyRow.title: Dependency decision row
dependencyRow.description: One candidate and the decision about it. Only decision, reason and toolchain are new; the rest is cat-harness DependsOnRecord and smart-base KG evidence. Once adjudicated, a reuse, adapt or extend row becomes an ordinary dependency: the DAK's own reference at L2, a sushi-config.yaml dependencies entry at L3. Defined by the l2-dependency-choice output contract and copied inline wherever it is passed on; the stage chain check compares the copies.

upstream.description: For a jurisdiction's adaptation: the packageId of the WHO original, recorded as its upstream.

evidence.description: The KG node ids that point at the candidate: L1 nodes at L2; L1 nodes and L2 assets at L3 (smart-base KG evidence).

decision.description: reuse: unchanged. adapt: fork and change. extend: depend and add. reject: not used.

reason.description: One sentence; required for reject (stated here rather than as if/then, which the conformance reader does not take).

id.description: A DAK component at L2 (personas, business-processes, ...); a profile, value set or library canonical at L3.

toolchain.description: For a component reused, adapted or extended: how the candidate produces it, so stages 4 and 6 produce it the same way. A Tool id from bun run cat check:tools, or a script in the candidate's own repository (its source spreadsheet, converter, CQL refresh, test format), found by the search in smart-base-tools section Adapting a DAK. none only after that search came back empty, naming where it looked; the new tool is then a Tool node, never a script in the adaptation repository.

components.description: What is taken from the candidate, piece by piece.

stagingLinks.title: Staging links
stagingLinks.description: The staging preview of the work a request for feedback is about: one deep link per changed page (the page and the anchor where the change sits) with the same page on main as `before`. Mirrors StagingComparison in schemas/staging.ts. The rule is skills/sdlc/sdlc-core/staging-review.md §"The deep-link rule". Copied inline as `definitions.stagingLinks` into every skill contract that carries it; schemas/staging.test.ts fails when a copy drifts.

slug.description: Branch slug used in the staging URL path.

pages.description: One entry per changed page, deep-linked; from the change's rendered-impact list, never chosen by judgement.

before.description: Same page on main; absent for a new page.

after.description: The page on the staging preview, with the anchor where the change sits; absent for a deleted page.

summary.description: What to look at on this page.

missing.description: What could not be linked, said rather than hidden: no preview yet (and when it will exist), no page list computed, or a changed page the publish ref does not hold.

stagingLinks.$comment: Copy of cat-harness schemas/staging-comparison.schema.json; cat-harness schemas/staging.test.ts fails when a copy drifts.
